Iran Is In No Hurry to Negotiate, Trump Chalked the Delay Up To Personal Animosity 

🔤🔤🔤🔤1️⃣

Iran, in the middle of an escalating five-month war with the US, continues to stumble from one internal crisis to another – whether it is over public executions, the rising cost of living, the alleged bias of the state broadcaster or even the post-midnight destruction of pavements outside liberal-leaning Tehran cafes. 

Very little that happens in Iran, cultural or political, momentous or trivial, does so uncontested.

But there is now a growing threat of a long diplomatic deadlock, forged by mutual distrust in which neither side believes the other will stick to any agreement. 

That impasse has occurred as the war broadens, drawing in Yemen, Iraq and now Egypt. In Iran, at least, the advocates of escalation are winning. As a result, a convergence of Iran’s conflicts, internal and external, becomes more likely.

Parts of the Trump administration and the Iranian opposition – including Reza Pahlavi, the son of the former deposed Shah – have never abandoned the belief that the Iranian government is on the brink of collapse.

What is true is that the picture of cohesive if brittle society presented by the millions attending the funeral of the supreme leader Ali Khamenei earlier this month revealed only one side of the public mood.

At a recent meeting of the supreme judicial council he argued: “Iran is engaged in a full-scale war. Today’s war is not just a war of missiles; the enemy has come to the conclusion that it cannot force the Iranian nation to surrender through military attacks. The most important battlefield today is the economy and livelihood of the people.

If economic pressures cause social discontent to form and this discontent spreads, the enormous social capital that the people have created in support of the system will be lost.”

Golshan Fathi, a Tehran human rights activist, recently wrote on her social media page: “The same sick cycle repeats (…) morning (…) the call to prayer, news of an execution (…) noon with power cuts, afternoon the water stops (…) dusk, the anxiety of war and renewed attacks on cities, and at midnight, the earth trembles.

Dissent in the form of political protest also exists, whether it is those inside jails or citizens in the squares of Isfahan protesting against the current wave of intimidatory public executions.

⚡️ Ethereum price has remained trapped below $2,000 as rising oil prices, renewed interest-rate concerns and BitMEX’s planned shutdown have tempered bullish sentiment despite continued spot ETF inflows. According to data from cryptonews, Ethereum price traded near $1,927 on July 23 after reaching an intraday high of $1,941. The token has recovered more than 27% from its June low near $1,514, but repeated failures around $1,955 have kept the psychological $2,000 level beyond buyers’ reach.

🔗 Rate traders have already adjusted their positions. The probability of a September Fed hike rose to 79% from 68% per data from the CME FedWatch tool. Expectations for the July meeting remain centered on no change, but another oil-led inflation increase could lift Treasury yields and pressure risk assets such as Ethereum.

THE NEXT USER MAY NOT BE HUMAN 🤖

For years, financial platforms were built for people.

A person opened an app.
A person selected an asset.
A person confirmed the transaction.

That model is beginning to change.

AI agents can now receive wallets, pay for digital services, trade assets and complete multi-step financial workflows within limits defined by their owners.

Coinbase reports that its x402 protocol processed more than 160 million agentic payments over the past year. It has also introduced tools that allow AI agents to trade, pay and execute workflows through a connected Coinbase account.

This creates a new type of market participant:

software that can analyse and act without waiting for every individual human command.

But autonomy without control is not intelligence.

Any financial agent needs:

• spending limits
• defined permissions
• approved assets and services
• complete transaction records
• the ability to stop execution immediately

The important question is not:

“Can an AI agent move money?”

It is:

“Under which rules is it allowed to act?”

This is the core principle of systematic finance.

Automation should not operate without boundaries.

It should execute faster inside a clearly defined structure.

The future may belong to autonomous financial agents.
Trust will still depend on the rules controlling them.

🌍 Eight Palestinians killed in Gaza; death toll nears 73,350

📌 Tehran, IRNA – At least eight Palestinians have been killed in the latest Israeli attacks on the Gaza Strip, bringing the total number of fatalities from the nearly three-year-long war to 73,349.

According to a statement by the Gaza Health Ministry, carried by Shehab News Agency on Saturday, eight Palestinians lost their lives and 76 others were wounded across the Gaza Strip over the past 24 hours.
​
Gaza’s total death toll has now reached 73,349, while the number of injured has risen to 174,162 since the beginning of the war on October 7, 2023, the ministry said.
​
It also put the number of fatalities and injuries at 1,222 and 4,053, respectively, since a ceasefire took effect between Hamas and Israel on October 11, 2025.
​
Israel has violated the ceasefire on an almost daily basis, restricting the entry of humanitarian aid into the Gaza Strip while continuing to launch deadly attacks on Palestinians there.
​
On Friday, the Palestinian Islamic Resistance Movement, Hamas, said that it and other Palestinian factions had engaged responsibly and constructively in negotiations and with proposals presented by mediators to complete the implementation of the second phase of the ceasefire agreement.
​
In a statement, Hamas stressed that the implementation of the second phase remains conditional on the Israeli regime honoring all of its obligations under the first phase of the agreement.
​
The movement said the Palestinian factions’ position reflects a national consensus and a shared commitment to protecting the Palestinian people, addressing urgent humanitarian needs, and safeguarding Palestinian national rights.
​
Hamas said ending the Israeli regime’s ongoing massacres and military aggression is the essential first step toward implementing the agreement and establishing a framework and timetable for carrying out its remaining provisions.
